title: Structures
summary: A struct groups named fields of different types into one value. Fields are reached with a dot, or with an arrow through a pointer. Structs are copied when assigned or passed, so large ones go by pointer. The compiler adds padding between fields so each one sits at an address that suits it.

cards.q: What does p->score mean when p is a struct pointer?
cards.a:
(*p).score

The arrow follows the pointer and picks the field.

cards.q: What happens when one struct variable is assigned to another?
cards.a:
Every field is copied, arrays inside included

Structs are values.

cards.q: Why can sizeof(struct) be bigger than the sum of its fields?
cards.a:
Padding is added to keep fields aligned

Reordering fields can reduce it.

cards.q: How do you compare two structs?
cards.a:
Field by field

C has no == for structs.
